- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, it often overcorrects; cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods of strong upward sentiment; apply a 3–5% upward bias to first 3–5 forecast days if sentiment > 0.1.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = previous + 0.5×(true - model) to avoid over-optimism.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.15), model often fails to capture trend persistence; use 3-day moving average of true values as anchor for next forecast.
